name: Kuru
certainty_note: The Kuru country of the upper Ganges–Yamunā doab and Kurukṣetra; broad agreement on the region, not its borders.

name: Pāñcāla
certainty_note: East of the Kurus along the Gaṅgā (Rohilkhand / central doab).

name: Matsya
certainty_note: King Virāṭa’s country, traditionally north-eastern Rajasthan (around Bairat).

name: Gāndhāra
certainty_note: Gāndhārī’s homeland in the north-west (Peshawar valley region).

name: Aṅga
certainty_note: Karṇa’s kingdom in the east (around Bhagalpur, Bihar).

name: Ānarta
certainty_note: The Yādava coast of the west (Saurāṣṭra / Gujarat).

name: Himavat
certainty_note: The Himālaya as the text names it.

name: Indrakīla
certainty_note: The mountain where Arjuna does penance; named in the text but not securely located.
desc: A mountain in the Himālaya where Arjuna does penance to win divine weapons. The Pāṇḍavas will make their last walk through these mountains.

name: Kāmyaka
certainty_note: Forest on the Sarasvatī; a tīrtha near Kurukṣetra carries the name today.
desc: The Kāmyaka forest near the Sarasvatī, one of the two forests of the Pāṇḍavas’ twelve-year exile.

name: Dvaitavana
certainty_note: Forest with a lake, near the Sarasvatī; its exact place is debated.
desc: The Dvaita forest and its lake, where the Pāṇḍavas live for much of their exile.

name: The Yakṣa’s Lake
certainty_note: A lake within Dvaitavana, as the text tells it.
desc: A still lake in the forest, guarded by a yakṣa who asks questions before anyone may drink.

name: Virāṭa’s City
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with Bairat (Viratnagar), Rajasthan.
desc: King Virāṭa’s capital, where the Pāṇḍavas live in disguise in their thirteenth year.

name: Upaplavya
certainty_note: A Matsya town named as the Pāṇḍavas’ war base; no agreed identification.
desc: A town of the Matsyas that becomes the Pāṇḍavas’ base as they prepare for war.

name: Dvārakā
certainty_note: Kṛṣṇa’s city on the western sea, as the text tells it.
desc: Kṛṣṇa’s city on the western sea, capital of the Yādavas.

name: Mathurā
certainty_note: Identified with modern Mathura.
desc: Kṛṣṇa’s birthplace on the Yamunā.

name: Mount Mahendra
certainty_note: Traditionally the Mahendragiri hills of the eastern coast.
desc: Paraśurāma’s retreat on Mount Mahendra, where Karṇa studied in disguise as a brahmin.

name: Pramāṇakoṭi on the Gaṅgā
certainty_note: The great banyan on the Gaṅgā where the exiles spend their first night; not located.
desc: A great banyan on the bank of the Gaṅgā where the exiles spend their first night out of Hastināpura.

name: Indraprastha
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with the Purana Qila mound, Delhi.
desc: The Pāṇḍavas’ own city, built from the Khāṇḍava forest.

name: Vāraṇāvata
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with Barnawa, Baghpat district.
desc: The town of the house of lac.

name: Hastināpura
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with Hastinapur, Meerut district.
desc: The Kuru capital on the Gaṅgā: the court, the palace, the river where Karṇa worships the sun.

name: Gaṅgā’s Bank
certainty_note: The river bank near the city, as the text tells it.
desc: The Gaṅgā near Hastināpura, where Karṇa offers worship to the sun each day — and where no one who asks him for a gift is refused.

name: Inner Palace, Hastināpura
certainty_note: Within the city, as the text tells it.
desc: The private quarters of the blind king Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Queen Gāndhārī.

name: Assembly Hall, Hastināpura
certainty_note: Within the city, as the text tells it.
desc: The royal assembly of the Kurus in Hastināpura: the throne, the elders, the court.

name: Kāmpilya
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with Kampil, Farrukhabad district.
desc: Drupada’s capital in southern Pāñcāla, where Draupadī’s svayaṃvara is held.

name: Ekacakrā
certainty_note: The village where Bhīma kills Baka; several identifications are proposed.
desc: The village where the Pāṇḍavas hide as brahmins after the house of lac.

name: Maṇipura
certainty_note: Citrāṅgadā’s kingdom; placed variously in the north-east or on the eastern coast.
desc: Citrāṅgadā’s kingdom, where Arjuna’s son Babhruvāhana is born.

name: Naimiṣa Forest
certainty_note: Traditionally identified with Nimsar (Naimisharanya), Sitapur district.
desc: The forest where Ugraśravas tells the whole epic to the sages: the frame of the story.

name: Kurukṣetra
certainty_note: The text places it between the Sarasvatī and the Dṛṣadvatī; tradition places it at modern Kurukshetra.
desc: The plain of Kurukṣetra, ‘the field of dharma’, where eighteen armies meet for eighteen days.

name: Pāṇḍava Camp
certainty_note: On the field, as the text tells it.
desc: The tents of the Pāṇḍava army at the edge of the battlefield.

name: Dvaipāyana Lake
certainty_note: Near the battlefield, as the text tells it.
desc: Dvaipāyana lake, where Duryodhana hides on the last day of the war.

name: Kaurava Camp
certainty_note: On the field, as the text tells it.
desc: The tents of the Kaurava army across the field.
